atomicPersistence.selection: Highest valid generation wins; different valid identities at the same highest generation fail with SNAPSHOT_GENERATION_CONFLICT.
atomicPersistence.composition: Atomic envelope validation calls reloadWorld(payload), so a selected snapshot may deterministically complete a pending non-canonical memory-compaction journal.

benchmark.boundary: Existing local scheduler/lifecycle microbenchmark only; atomic persistence, fsync, process-exit recovery, deferred-mailbox, and compaction-recovery timing are not measured.

claimBoundary: The atomic persistence proof uses abrupt process exit on GitHub Actions Ubuntu 24.04, not sudden power loss.
AFTER_TEMP_WRITE occurs before file fsync; its success proves only that the valid temp survived the tested process exit.
Directory fsync is required by default, but behavior across every operating system and filesystem is not established.
There is no single-writer lock, lease, or fencing token yet.
The immediate parent snapshot ID is recorded; complete historical chain verification is not implemented.
The API does not yet provide one admission transaction spanning world mutation, scheduler queue, deferred mailbox, and compaction journal.
Automatic recovery is not possible when every local candidate is invalid.
No production-scale or massive-world performance claim is established.
Specialists remain proposal-only and are not independent workers.
